title: G6: stop ack for prior session kills newly-started Sensor row
body:
### Subject of the issue
Link to the discussion thread: https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/discussions/2635

When changing a sensor on a G6, if xDrip's queued `SessionStopTxMessage` hasn't actually been transmitted to the G6 yet by the time the user starts a new sensor session, the eventual stop ack from the transmitter kills the newly-created `Sensors` row instead of the one it is actually confirming stopped. The result is no BG values on the main screen or broadcast after warmup completes, even though the G6 detail view and the internal state machine show the new session running normally.

### Your environment
- xDrip version: a32f1c4-2026.05.06 (current master at the time of report)
- Hardware data source: Dexcom G6 native (Ob1G5 collection, transmitter algorithm)
- Confirmed on two phones in the same household: Pixel 8 Pro / Android 16, plus a second Android phone with the same xDrip build
- Settings: `ob1_g5_use_transmitter_alg` enabled, `ob1_g5_restart_sensor` disabled (the auto-restart code path is unaffected by this bug)

### Expected behavior
After stopping a sensor in xDrip and then starting a new one before the queued stop has actually reached the transmitter, the new session should remain active in xDrip once the queued stop is finally transmitted and acknowledged. The main screen and broadcast should continue showing the new session through warmup and into live BG values.

### Actual behavior
Once the queued stop is finally transmitted and the G6 confirms "sensor stopped":

- The main screen reverts to "Please start sensor".
- The detailed G6 view continues to show the correct state (warmup countdown, then "started") - the state machine in `Ob1G5StateMachine` is unaffected.
- xDrip's `Sensors` table no longer has an active row.
- Even after the full warmup completes, no BG values appear on the main screen and nothing is sent to broadcast. The transmitter keeps producing readings but they go nowhere.

The only recovery is to click "Start Sensor" again from the menu. This calls `Sensor.create()` and re-syncs the database with the transmitter's actual state. The duplicate `SessionStartTxMessage` is silently ignored by the transmitter.

### Steps to reproduce the behavior
1. Select "Stop Sensor" in xDrip. This queues a `SessionStopTxMessage` but doesn't actually send it to the transmitter until the next BLE connection window (up to ~5 minutes).
2. Place a new sensor.
3. Select "Start Sensor", acknowledge the popup, enter the calibration code. The main screen shows "Starting transmitter" with a countdown.
4. The queued stop is finally transmitted. xDrip receives "sensor stopped" from the transmitter and immediately sends the queued start on the next BLE cycle.
5. Main screen reverts to "Please start sensor". The Sensor row that was created in step 3 has been killed.

### Where it's happening
In `Ob1G5CollectionService.processCalibrationState` (around line 1990), when the transmitter reports it has stopped (`!is_started && was_started`), the code calls `Sensor.stopSensor()` on whatever is the active Sensor row. By the time the queued STOP is actually transmitted and acknowledged, "currently active" is the new session the user just started in step 3, not the prior one the transmitter is confirming stopped. So the new row gets killed.

The state machine in `Ob1G5StateMachine` isn't affected (it tracks the physical transmitter session, which is why the detailed view stays correct). The damage is only to the `Sensors` table. The existing auto-heal in `Ob1G5StateMachine.checkAndActivateSensor` would re-create a row when the transmitter starts producing readings, but its `!Sensor.stoppedRecently()` guard blocks it for 2 hours (unless we would be on G7 which is gated by the short ID), which covers the entire warmup.

The log line is `Marking sensor session as stopped` from `Ob1G5CollectionService` (same as reported in discussion #2635).

### Evidence
Across two phones in our household, the bug is visible everywhere in the `Sensors` table: a row with a lifespan of 0.1 - 25 min (cannot be a real session), immediately preceded by another stopped row in `_id` order, often followed by another fresh row a few minutes later (the second Start click as workaround).

| phone | history | sessions | occurrences |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ~2 years | 93 | 14 (15%) |
| 2 | ~2.7 years | 182 | 56 (31%) |

Both phones show this happening 1-3 times every month, consistently across the entire history.

### Proposed fix
When processing the stop ack, check `Ob1G5StateMachine.pendingStart()`. If a `SessionStartTxMessage` is already queued, the user has moved past the session the transmitter is confirming stopped: leave the current Sensor row alone and suppress the redundant "Sensor Stopped" notification/treatment entry.

Patch on https://github.com/savek-cc/xDrip/tree/fix/preserve-sensor-row-on-stale-stop-ack in my fork. Will validate on both devices before opening an upstream PR.

Also previously discussed (without resolution) in NightscoutFoundation/xDrip#1412 and NightscoutFoundation/xDrip#1632.
